Issued at 1237 AM CDT Fri Aug 14 2026

This Morning: Heavy Rainfall Potential

A surface boundary remains situated across central Iowa into 
northern Illinois early this morning as 850hPa warm advection and 
moisture transport nose into it, providing a source of lift for 
convective development through the morning hours. The environment 
along this boundary remains favorable for heavy rainfall as PWATs 
above the 90th percentile of climatology exist across the region, 
warm cloud depths exceed 10kft, and storm motion vectors parallel 
the boundary, favorable for training storms. While the heaviest rain 
is expected across central Iowa and northern Illinois within the 
vicinity of the boundary and in the region of higher instability,
CAM solutions to suggest precipitation makes its way northward 
into our portions of northeast Iowa and southwest Wisconsin 
through this morning. Probabilities of precipitation across 
these regions sit around 40-60% though probabilities for 1 inch 
or greater are far lower and have trended southward as compared 
to 12 hours ago, generally 10-20% at most per the 14.00z HREF. 
That said, there's also remains some uncertainty in how far 
north rainfall is actually able to make it given the current 
position of the surface boundary and little in the way of 
synoptic forcing to shift it northward. 

This Afternoon - Saturday: Additional Heavy Rainfall Potential

Through this afternoon, there is some suggestion of scattered shower 
activity across the area, primarily for those along and south of I-
90, as some areas of maximized 850hPa moisture transport nudge into 
the Upper Mississippi River Valley. Many CAM solutions do highlight 
this potential with the 14.00z HREF suggesting probabilities sit 
around 10-30%. Amounts with any showers would be light, generally on 
the order of 0.1 inches. 

Heading into this evening and tonight, the upper level ridge axis 
located over much of the United States builds northward slightly 
while another 500hPa shortwave moves eastward across the Midwest. 
The boundary associated with this morning's rainfall also remains 
somewhere across Iowa and Illinois throughout the day, though where 
exactly it situates itself is somewhat uncertain. Regardless, 
another round of heavy rainfall looks likely along the boundary as 
the wave moves through given a very similar set-up to this morning. 
With the northward trend of the upper ridge and 850hPa moisture 
transport/warm advection by association, there is some potential for 
this round of heavy rain to make its way into those areas mainly 
along and south of Highway 18 (60-80%) and perhaps towards I-90 (30-
60%). That said, the 14.00z HRRR solution suggests that any activity 
will largely remain south of our area, primarily along and south of 
I-80. Curious if the majority of the model suites are somewhat too 
far north with precipitation potential given the several rounds of 
rain across the region over the last few days and a more HRRR-like 
solution would be more likely, though given the consensus 
regarding the northward trend, there is currently higher 
confidence in this more northern solution regarding rainfall 
potential tonight. Fortunately, amounts look to be far less 
impressive than they have been for those across central Iowa 
into Illinois. Probabilities for amounts of 1 inch or more sit 
around 30-60% in the 14.00z HREF with some members suggesting a 
few pockets around 2 inches could occur per the LPMM. 

Rainfall largely shifts eastward through Saturday morning resulting 
in primarily dry conditions through the afternoon. However, there is 
some low potential for some scattered showers through the afternoon 
hours as another shortwave moves through the region. 

Sunday - Mid Week: Briefly Drier, Additional Shower/Storm Chances

The upper level ridge begins to break down and retrograde on Sunday 
as a jet streak and associated trough along the US/Canada border 
translate eastward. A weak surface front moves through the Upper 
Midwest along with these upper level features while high pressure 
sinks southward behind the front. Can't completely rule out some 
scattered showers south of I-90 Sunday afternoon as this boundary 
moves through the region, though there's quite a bit of discrepancy 
within the ensemble suites as far as timing and location of 
precipitation is concerned. Because of this, the 14.01z NBM suggests 
probabilities for precipitation during this period are 20-30%. 
Heading into Sunday night and Monday, a drier period looks to be in 
store for the region as the high pressure takes a stronger hold over 
the region, though this will be short-lived as deterministic models 
suggest another shortwave trough and associated surface front move 
through the region by the middle of next week bringing additional 
showers and storms (50-70%).
